chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

Banu Isra'il used to be such that when a drop of urine struck one of them, they would cut their flesh with scissors. But Allah has granted you vast ease, as vast as what lies between the heaven and the earth, and He has made water a purifier for you, so consider how you will be.

key_terms.الْمَاءَ: Water, the means Allah made available for purification.
key_terms.الْمَقَارِيضِ: Scissors, the instrument by which they cut the affected flesh.
key_terms.بَنُو إِسْرَائِيلَ: The Children of Israel, mentioned here as an earlier community with stricter purity burdens.
key_terms.طَهُورًا: A purifier, meaning that by it ritual purification is achieved.
key_terms.قَرَضُوا: They cut away, describing the severity of their former practice.
key_terms.قَطْرَةُ بَوْلٍ: A drop of urine, referring to ritual impurity requiring purification.
key_terms.وَسَّعَ: He gave spacious ease, indicating Allah’s leniency and breadth of allowance.

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain Allah’s ease in the laws of ritual purity compared with Banu Isra'il?
ai.summary: This hadith contrasts the severe purity burdens placed upon Banu Isra'il with the ease Allah has granted this Ummah through taharah by water. It teaches gratitude, careful observance of ritual purity, and awareness that divine leniency should lead to better conduct, not negligence.
